function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.content:
**Java** is a high‑level, object‑oriented programming language and computing platform that was first released by Sun Microsystems in 1995 (now owned by Oracle). It’s designed to be:

| Feature | What it means |
|---------|---------------|
| **Write once, run anywhere (WORA)** | Java programs compile to bytecode that runs on any device with a Java Virtual Machine (JVM), regardless of the underlying hardware or operating system. |
| **Object‑oriented** | Everything is an object (except primitives), encouraging modular, reusable code. |
| **Strongly typed & safe** | The compiler checks types at compile time, and the JVM enforces memory safety (no direct pointer manipulation). |
| **Platform‑independent runtime** | The JVM interprets or just‑in‑time compiles bytecode into native machine code at runtime. |
| **Rich standard library** | Includes collections, networking, I/O, concurrency, GUI (Swing/JavaFX), and many other APIs. |
| **Enterprise‑ready** | Widely used for web servers, enterprise applications (Java EE / Jakarta EE), microservices, and big‑data frameworks (Hadoop, Spark). |
| **Open‑source implementations** | Besides Oracle’s JDK, there are OpenJDK, AdoptOpenJDK, Amazon Corretto, etc. |

### Typical Java ecosystem components

| Component | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|
| **JDK (Java Development Kit)** | Toolchain for compiling (`javac`) and running (`java`) Java programs. |
| **JRE (Java Runtime Environment)** | Runtime only – includes the JVM and core libraries. |
| **JVM (Java Virtual Machine)** | Executes bytecode, handles memory management, garbage collection, and thread scheduling. |
| **Build tools** | Maven, Gradle, Ant – manage dependencies, build lifecycle, and packaging. |
| **IDE** | IntelliJ IDEA, Eclipse, NetBeans – provide code completion, debugging, and project management. |

### Common use cases

- **Desktop applications** (Swing, JavaFX)
- **Web applications** (Servlets, JSP, Spring MVC, Jakarta EE)
- **Microservices** (Spring Boot, Micronaut)
- **Mobile** (Android uses Java‑like syntax, though Kotlin is now preferred)
- **Big data & analytics** (Apache Hadoop, Apache Spark)
- **Embedded systems** (Java ME, Java SE Embedded)

### Quick example

```java
public class HelloWorld {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        System.out.println("Hello, Java!");
    }
}
```

Compile with `javac HelloWorld.java` and run with `java HelloWorld`. The same bytecode will run on Windows, macOS, Linux, or any JVM‑capable device.

---

In short, Java is a versatile, mature language and runtime that powers everything from small utilities to massive enterprise systems, all while keeping the “write once, run anywhere” promise.
